title: Site area merit assessment criteria
text: M4.1.1 Development of the type and density indicated by the density code designated in the scheme. M4.1.2 The WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a green title lot, survey-strata lot or strata lot with an average site area up to 5 per cent less than that specified in Table 4B where it will: i. facilitate the protection of an environmental or heritage feature; ii. facilitate the retention of a significant element that contributes toward an existing streetscape worthy of retention; iii. facilitate the development of lots with separate and sufficient frontage to more than one public street; iv. overcome a special or unusual limitation on the development of the land imposed by its size, shape or other feature; v. allow land to be developed with housing of the same type and form as land in the vicinity and which would not otherwise be able to be developed; or vi. achieve specific objectives of the local planning framework. [Potential change: Local governments to have ability to approve variations to minimum and/or average site area up to 5 per cent through a development approval.] M4.1.3 Notwithstanding M4.1.2, for apartments in areas coded R40 - R60; the decision-maker may approve a development application involving the creation of a strata lot of a lesser average site area than that specified in Table 4B provided that the proposed variation does not limit the ability for the development to achieve the relevant provisions of the R-Codes, and will: i. facilitate housing and dwelling diversity; ii. facilitate the protection of an environmental or heritage feature; iii. facilitate the retention of a significant element that contributes toward an existing streetscape worthy of retention; iv. allow land to be developed with housing of the same types and form as land in the vicinity and which would not otherwise be able to be developed; or v. achieve specific objectives of the local planning framework. M4.1.4 The WAPC, in consultation with the local government, may approve the creation of a survey-strata lot or strata lot for an existing authorised grouped dwelling or apartment development of a lesser minimum and average site area than that specified in Table 4B, where, in the opinion of the WAPC or the local government, the development on the resulting survey-strata or strata lots is consistent with the objectives of the relevant design elements of the R-Codes, and the orderly and proper planning of the locality.

replaces.note: M4.1.3 R40-R60 strata lot variation; potential-change box

notes: from: ch3 M4.1. diverges: M4.1.2 average only (no minimum, strata lots included); M4.1.3 is the new R40-R60 decision-maker variation; M4.1.4 covers apartments; no corner-lot (ch3 M4.1.3) or retained-dwelling potential changes. M4.1.2 to M4.1.4 and the potential-change box are also recorded one per file under rules/4.1 (column M). Maisonette / low-scale apartments in R10-R25 (C4P1-149): no draft provision; Information Sheet 5 seeks feedback only, so Table 4B R10-R25 averages remain.
